title: GPU SKU phased onboarding and transport constraints log
summary: Working log for phased onboarding of new GPU SKUs with an emphasis on transport constraints, customs risk, and regional staging capacity. Contains assumptions, phased order plan, contingency lanes, burn-in requirements, and unresolved questions for next supplier sync.
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a living planning sheet capturing the operational details for a phased onboarding of three new GPU SKUs (A100-80GB-Q, H100-80GB-Q, and L4-32GB-Q) across US-W, EU-N, and APAC-S regions. Primary objective: minimize downtime/latency regressions while keeping inventory exposure low and avoiding large single-shipment customs/port bottlenecks.

High-level approach (phased onboarding):
1) Phase 0 — Pilot batch (small footprint): 8 units per SKU to a single region (US-W) for burn-in and perf verification within Redwood staging cluster.
2) Phase 1 — Regional stagger: follow-up shipments to EU-N and APAC-S with smaller batches (12–16 units) after pilot metrics satisifed (latency, temperature, failure rate).
3) Phase 2 — Capacity scale: bulk orders for Dedicated capacity and replenishment of host pools after measured utilization and forecast demand signals.

Why phased: reduces customs/transport risk per shipment, gives time to validate kernel/path optimizations, enables early model-variant fallback testing.

Transport constraints and key assumptions:
- Typical OEM lead time (PLT) from PO to factory ready: 8–12 weeks (SKU-specific).
- Sea freight (cheapest) from manufacturer hub to EU-N: 6–8 weeks door-to-door with customs; port congestion margin +2 weeks during peak season.
- Air freight to US-W: 3–6 days nominal, but current charters and capacity issues add up to 2 weeks to schedule in Q3/Q4.
- APAC intra-region shipments often take 1–2 weeks by truck/freight but cross-border customs can add 5–10 business days.
- Local import clearance variance: EU-N typically predictable (2–4 business days), APAC-S depends heavily on paperwork — treat as 1–3 week stochastic variable.

Operational constraints noted in recent supplier calls:
- Supplier batch windows top out at 48 units per production run per SKU. If we need >48/region in a 30-day window, we must split across multiple runs and expect +4–6 week cumulative lead time.
- Packaging adjustments (racks vs crates) add 1–2 weeks to ship prep. Rack-ready units reduce onsite staging time but increase OEM prep time.
- Customs documentation mismatch observed for one past shipment (missing KCs in APAC-S) — recommend pre-clearance checklist attached to PO.

Phased order plan (working numbers):
- Pilot PO (sent): 2025-02-15: 3 SKU types x 8 units = 24 units to US-W via air (charter request).
- Phase 1 tentative POs (targeted booking week): 2025-03-15: EU-N 14 units per SKU by sea (stagger arrivals every 2 weeks), APAC-S 12 units per SKU by air+truck.
- Phase 2 bulk (forecast commit window): 2025-06-01: US-W reserve 120 units total across SKUs; EU-N 80 units; APAC-S 60 units (mix flexible).
Note: Phase 2 subject to utilization triggers in the capacity forecasting workbook (linked).

Inventory math and buffer policy (rules of thumb):
- Burn-in and QA: allocate 5% of incoming units for rack-level burn and initial failure triage. Expect ~1–2 DOA failures per 100 units (historical).
- Operational buffer: maintain 4 weeks of equivalent production burn (measured as average weekly token-hour capacity consumption).
- Safety stock: SKU-specific safety stock = max(2 weeks forecast demand, 1 production run size/2). This keeps reorder points from creating single-run dependency.

Sample lead-time sensitivity (toy calc):
- If OEM PLT = 10 weeks and sea freight = 8 weeks, end-to-end = 18 weeks + customs variance (±2 weeks). That means reorder signals should ideally be sent when runway <= 20 weeks.
- For air freight emergency lane (cost x3), effective end-to-end ~3 weeks. Reserve emergency capex budget and vendor pre-approval for air lanes.

Transport lanes and contingency matrix (short):
- Preferred lane EU-N: sea -> inland rail -> bonded warehouse. Contingency: send smaller air shipments for critical racks if sea backlog >2 weeks.
- Preferred lane US-W: air direct to SFO/LAX bonded (fast). Contingency: move to West US secondary port and truck if airport slot unknown.
- Preferred lane APAC-S: consolidated air for pilot; contingency: regional brokers with local hand-carry for small batches.

Staging & rack build notes:
- Recommend minimum staging footprint for pilot: 2 racks (42U) with power/cooling test capability. Build-out time per rack: ~3 business days if parts on-hand, +7–10 days if sourced.
- Rack-integrated burn-in script: 48–72 hours of synthetic token runs at sampling rate 0.5x production to flush early failures.

Quality gates and rollout triggers (must all be green to move on):
- Gate 1 (pilot acceptance): <1% critical hardware failures during burn, latency metrics within 10% of baseline for 95th percentile.
- Gate 2 (regional acceptance): regional telemetry stable for 7 days under canary traffic (A/B rollout).
- Gate 3 (scale): replication tests for KV cache and batching under 2x expected peak for 1 hour sustained.

Cost vs speed trade-offs (notes to finance):
- Air freight spike multiplier assumed x3–6 vs sea. Factor into expedited order approvals.
- Leasing short-term capacity (GPU spot leases) may be cheaper for 4–8 week gaps vs premium air. Recommend a decision matrix for >$60k expedited shipping per PO.

Open questions / unresolved items (action owners inline):
- Who signs emergency air lane approvals? (action: @Marco Rivera — confirm delegated approver list)
- APAC-S customs broker: confirm local partner with experience for electronics (action: @Lena Hofmann to shortlist by 2025-03-07).
- Rack vs crate cost breakup from OEM: request updated quote including rack-assembly time (action: @Samir Khan — PR to vendor).
- Should we pre-approve one supplier for cross-region transfer between EU-N and APAC-S in case of redistribution need? (ops design decision)

Quick wins identified:
- Add a pre-clearance checklist item to every PO noting country-specific KCs and inbound customs doc owner.
- Reserve a single small air-charter slot per quarter as a burst lane; cost amortized across multiple emergency usages.
- Add a transient lease line to budget to cover temporary capacity gaps during long lead-time windows.

Appendix (short tables represented inline):
- Planned pilot burn schedule:
  * Week 0 (arrival): unpack + rack mount = 2 days
  * Week 0–1: burn-in scripts (48–72h) + firmware updates + kernel test
  * Week 1–2: canary with 5% live traffic, telemetry collection
  * Week 2: decision meeting (green -> proceed; red -> hold + vendor triage)

- SKU lead-time rough table (working):
  * A100-80GB-Q: OEM PLT 9–11 weeks, sea 7–9 weeks, air 1 week, packaging prep +1
  * H100-80GB-Q: OEM PLT 10–12 weeks, sea 8–10 weeks, air 1–2 days nominal, packaging prep +2
  * L4-32GB-Q: OEM PLT 6–8 weeks, sea 5–7 weeks, air 3–5 days, packaging prep +1

Meeting notes snapshot (2025-02-20 supplier sync):
- Supplier confirmed monthly production cap per SKU and ability to priority slot one run per quarter if we prepay a 10% expedite premium.
- They recommended combining packaging steps for EU and US to reduce prep time but warned about customs label differences introducing rework.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep Phase 0 deliberately small; we learned last year that large single shipments created a 6-week idle queue while customs paperwork sorted. Avoid that.
- Document handoffs: add owner column in the PO tracker for customs docs, local broker, and rack build.

Next steps (near-term):
- Finalize APAC broker shortlist (Lena) by 2025-03-07.
- Confirm emergency charter budget and approver list (Marco) by 2025-03-10.
- Request rack-ready vs crate-ready quotes from suppliers and log prep time differences (Samir) by 2025-03-12.

End of working log entry.
notes_to_self: Remember to transpose key metrics into capacity-forecast sheet and tag the PO tracker rows with phase and lane. Follow up with vendor for the rack-ready lead time detail.
